title: confed instance result
description: The `result` of every `confed instance … --json` command. `action` names the subcommand. Commands that run in several spaces (status, fetch, pull, push, doctor, clone) put one entry per space in `spaces`; `mv` and `resume` describe the move; `locate` and `tree` list pages in `pages`.

spaces.description: One entry per space, ordered by key. For status, fetch, pull, push and doctor, `result` is exactly that command's own result in that workspace, as described by its schema. `instance spaces` lists rows of its table here instead.

instance.description: `doctor`: the checks that span spaces (registration, pages tracked twice, unfinished moves, pages in another space on the server), as doctor.schema.json describes checks.

journal_id.description: `mv`, `resume`: the journal entry of the move; what `confed instance resume` and `abort` take.

moved.description: `mv`, `resume`: every page of the moved subtree, parent first. Before the move (a dry run) `version` is null.

page_id.description: Unchanged by the move. Null for a file that was never pushed, moved as a file.

links_rewritten.description: `mv`, `resume`: pages whose links confed rewrote on the server, each as one new version.

links_broken.description: `mv`, `resume`: links the move concerns that reach no page, left as they were.

space.description: The space of the page the link is in.

reaches.description: The space it looks for the title in.

links_by_server.description: `mv`, `resume`: pages whose links the server had already fixed itself.

warnings.description: `mv`, `resume`: restrictions that move with the pages, a rules page in the subtree, links the server updated. Also in the envelope's `warnings`.

roots.description: `mv`, `resume`: the pages moved, each with the pages under it, in the order they end up side by side under the destination. One plan, one journal entry.

summary.description: `mv`, `resume`: counts over the plan, for a move too large to read page by page.

renamed.description: `mv`, `resume`: every page whose title the move changes (or changed), and why. Pages under a renamed page are not in it: their paths change, their titles do not.

blocking.description: `mv`: what stops the move, each problem once. The rest of the result is the whole plan all the same; the exit code is 7 and nothing was written, on the server or in the journal.

existing_page_id.description: `title_taken`: the destination's page with that title.

suggested_title.description: `title_taken`: what `--on-conflict suffix` would call the page, when that title is free.

pulled.description: `mv`: pages the move named (the destination, pages beside it, the pages moved) that no workspace had yet, pulled before planning, and only those.

verified.description: `mv`, `resume`: what the move left, read back at its end. Null in a dry run.

at_destination.description: Moved pages tracked in the destination and in no other workspace.

source_remaining.description: Pages still tracked in the source, by path: the first 20.

workspaces_clean.description: Every page in both workspaces is unchanged.

pages.description: `locate`: one entry per page named, in order; `found` is false for one that was not, and its error is in the envelope's `errors`. `tree`: the pages under the page named (or the whole space), parent first, `depth` 0 for its children. `mv`: the plan's pages.

space.description: `create`: the space created, or with `dry_run` the one that would be. `tree`: the key of the space listed.

planned.description: `create --dry-run`: what would be done, one sentence per step.

dir.description: `create --dry-run`: the workspace the space would be cloned into, relative to the root; null with `--no-clone`.

cloned.description: `create`: where the new space was cloned, as `instance clone KEY` does it. Null with `--no-clone`, or when the clone failed: then `errors` has `kind: clone_failed`, the exit code is 8, and `confed instance clone KEY` finishes it.

clone.description: `create`, when the clone failed: the space's entry as `instance clone` reports it.

permissions.description: `create --permissions-from`: what was granted in the new space, as `confed admin perms copy` reports it (admin.schema.json), and the groups made for it. Under `--dry-run`, what would be. Null when the copy could not run at all after the space was created: then `errors` has `kind: permissions_failed`. A subject that failed alone has `ok: false` in `copied` and its own entry in `errors`; either way the exit code is 8 and `confed admin perms copy --from SRC --to KEY` finishes it.

groups_created.description: The groups `--create-groups` made, each with the members of the group it was mapped from.

cancelled.description: `create`: the confirmation was declined; nothing was created.

blocked.description: `mv`: why this server cannot make the move, when everything else checked out. The plan is still in the result to read; the exit code is 9 and nothing was written.

created_space.description: A space as the server has it after the create.

id.description: The server's numeric id, as a string like every confed id.

home_page_id.description: The home page the server made with the space.

url.description: The space in the browser: `…/display/KEY` on Data Center, `…/spaces/KEY` on Cloud.

planned_space.description: `--dry-run`: the space that would be created.

checks.description: `--dry-run`: what the server said before anything was created. Each check that fails is also an entry in the envelope's `errors`, with its `kind`, and the exit code is 7.

key_free.description: False when a space has the key: current, archived or personal (`kind: key_taken`). A space this account cannot see is only found by the create itself.

may_create.description: Whether this account may create spaces (`kind: no_permission` when false); null when the server would not say. Data Center has no API for it, so confed sends a create with the key `!`, which no server accepts, and reads whether it was refused for the permission or for the key.

dir.description: The workspace, relative to the instance root.

status.description: `clone`: what became of the space. `spaces --remote`: the space's status on the server, `current` or `archived`.

name.description: `spaces`: the space's name, as last fetched or, with `--remote`, as the server has it.

cloned.description: `spaces`: whether its workspace is in this root.

errors.description: Why the space failed; also in the envelope's `errors`, prefixed with the key.
